title.de: Bedingungen: if it rains, I'll stay
title.sl: Pogoji: if it rains, I'll stay
title.it: Le condizioni: if it rains, I'll stay

goal.sl: Poveš, kar velja vedno (If you heat butter, it melts), kaj bo, če se nekaj zgodi (If it rains, I'll stay), in kaj narediš, ko nekaj pride, s sedanjikom za if in when.
goal.de: Du sagst, was immer gilt (If you heat butter, it melts), was geschieht, wenn etwas passiert (If it rains, I'll stay), und was du machst, wenn etwas kommt, mit dem Präsens nach if und when.
goal.it: Dici ciò che vale sempre (If you heat butter, it melts), che cosa succede se capita qualcosa (If it rains, I'll stay) e che cosa farai quando arriva qualcosa, con il presente dopo if e when.
goal.en: You can say what is always so (If you heat butter, it melts), what will happen if something happens (If it rains, I'll stay), and what you'll do when something comes, with the present after if and when.

say.sl: Kar velja vedno: **if** (če) + sedanjik v obeh delih. **If you heat butter, it melts.** (Če maslo segreješ, se stopi.) **If it rains, the beck rises.** (Če dežuje, potok naraste.) **If the sheep are hungry, they come down.** (Če so ovce lačne, pridejo dol.) Vsakič je enako. **when** (ko) gre tu enako: **When it rains, the beck rises.** (Ko dežuje, potok naraste.)
say.de: Was immer gilt: **if** (wenn) + Präsens in beiden Teilen. **If you heat butter, it melts.** (Wenn man Butter erhitzt, schmilzt sie.) **If it rains, the beck rises.** (Wenn es regnet, steigt der Bach.) **If the sheep are hungry, they come down.** (Wenn die Schafe hungrig sind, kommen sie herunter.) Es ist jedes Mal so. **when** geht hier genauso: **When it rains, the beck rises.** (Wenn es regnet, steigt der Bach.)
say.it: Ciò che vale sempre: **if** (se) + il presente in tutte e due le parti. **If you heat butter, it melts.** (Se scaldi il burro, si scioglie.) **If it rains, the beck rises.** (Se piove, il ruscello sale.) **If the sheep are hungry, they come down.** (Se le pecore hanno fame, scendono.) È così ogni volta. **when** (quando) qui va allo stesso modo: **When it rains, the beck rises.** (Quando piove, il ruscello sale.)
say.en: What is always so: **if** + the present in both halves. **If you heat butter, it melts.** **If it rains, the beck rises.** **If the sheep are hungry, they come down.** It's the same every time. **when** works the same here: **When it rains, the beck rises.**

say.sl: Kar se lahko zgodi: **if** + sedanjik, **will** v drugem delu. **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** (Če bo deževalo, bom {m:ostal|f:ostala} doma.) **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** (Če bo Jack prišel, bomo pili čaj.) **If you're late, you'll miss the bus.** (Če zamudiš, ti bo avtobus ušel.) Za if nikoli will, čeprav slovenščina reče *če bo*: **If it rains**, nikoli *If it will rain*.
say.de: Was passieren kann: **if** + Präsens, **will** im anderen Teil. **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** (Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause.) **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** (Wenn Jack kommt, trinken wir Tee.) **If you're late, you'll miss the bus.** (Wenn du zu spät kommst, verpasst du den Bus.) Nach if nie will: **If it rains**, nie *If it will rain*.
say.it: Ciò che può succedere: **if** + il presente, **will** nell'altra parte. **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** (Se piove, resto a casa.) **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** (Se viene Jack, prendiamo il tè.) **If you're late, you'll miss the bus.** (Se fai tardi, perdi l'autobus.) Dopo if mai will, anche se l'italiano può dire *se pioverà*: **If it rains**, mai *If it will rain*.
say.en: What may happen: **if** + the present, **will** in the other half. **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** **If you're late, you'll miss the bus.** After if, no will: **If it rains** (never *If it will rain*).

ask.text: If it ___ (rain) tomorrow, I'll stay at home.

explain.sl:
**Za if: sedanjik, ne will**
- If it rains, I'll stay at home.
explain.de:
**Nach if: Präsens, nicht will**
- If it rains, I'll stay at home.
explain.it:
**Dopo if: il presente, non will**
- If it rains, I'll stay at home.
explain.en:
**After if: the present, not will**
- If it rains, I'll stay at home.

say.sl: Dela lahko zamenjata mesti: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** (Doma bom {m:ostal|f:ostala}, če bo deževalo.) Če je **if** prvi, je vejica, če je drugi, je ni. Zanikanje je kot običajno: **If Jack doesn't come, we'll go without him.** (Če Jack ne bo prišel, gremo brez njega.) **We won't go if it snows.** (Ne gremo, če bo snežilo.) Pri vprašanju gre will pred osebek: **What will you do if it snows?** (Kaj boš {m:naredil|f:naredila}, če bo snežilo?)
say.de: Die Teile können tauschen: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** (Ich bleibe zu Hause, wenn es regnet.) Steht **if** vorn, kommt ein Komma, steht es hinten, keines. Verneint wie immer: **If Jack doesn't come, we'll go without him.** (Wenn Jack nicht kommt, gehen wir ohne ihn.) **We won't go if it snows.** (Wir gehen nicht, wenn es schneit.) Bei der Frage kommt will vor das Subjekt: **What will you do if it snows?** (Was machst du, wenn es schneit?)
say.it: Le due parti possono scambiarsi: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** (Resto a casa se piove.) Con **if** all'inizio c'è la virgola, con **if** dopo no. Il negativo è quello di sempre: **If Jack doesn't come, we'll go without him.** (Se Jack non viene, andiamo senza di lui.) **We won't go if it snows.** (Non andiamo se nevica.) Per chiedere, will va prima del soggetto: **What will you do if it snows?** (Che cosa farai se nevica?)
say.en: The halves can change places: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** With **if** first there is a comma; with **if** second, none. Not works as usual: **If Jack doesn't come, we'll go without him.** **We won't go if it snows.** To ask, will goes before the subject: **What will you do if it snows?**

say.sl: **if** (če) je za to, kar se morda zgodi, **when** (ko) za to, kar se bo zgodilo: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** (Če bom {m:videl|f:videla} Jacka, mu povem.) **When I get home, I'll call you.** (Ko pridem domov, te pokličem.) Tudi za **when** pride sedanjik: **When it stops raining, we'll go out.** (Ko bo nehalo deževati, gremo ven.) Nikoli *When it will stop raining*.
say.de: **if** steht für das, was vielleicht geschieht, **when** für das, was sicher kommt; Deutsch sagt für beides *wenn*: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** (Falls ich Jack sehe, sage ich es ihm.) **When I get home, I'll call you.** (Wenn ich heimkomme, rufe ich dich an.) Auch nach **when** steht das Präsens: **When it stops raining, we'll go out.** (Wenn es aufhört zu regnen, gehen wir hinaus.) Nie *When it will stop raining*.
say.it: **if** (se) è per ciò che forse succede, **when** (quando) per ciò che succederà: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** (Se vedo Jack, glielo dico.) **When I get home, I'll call you.** (Quando arrivo a casa, ti chiamo.) Anche dopo **when** ci vuole il presente, dove l'italiano può dire *quando smetterà*: **When it stops raining, we'll go out.** (Quando smette di piovere, usciamo.) Mai *When it will stop raining*.
say.en: **if** is for what may happen, **when** for what will happen: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** (perhaps I will) **When I get home, I'll call you.** (I will get home) After **when**, the present too: **When it stops raining, we'll go out** (never *When it will stop raining*).

say.sl: Drugi del ni nujno z **will**. Lahko naroči ali ponudi: **If you see Jack, tell him.** (Če vidiš Jacka, mu povej.) **If you're tired, we can stop.** (Če si {m:utrujen|f:utrujena}, se lahko ustavimo.) **If you want to walk, you should take a map.** (Če hočeš peš, vzemi zemljevid.) Del z **if** ostane v sedanjiku.
say.de: Der andere Teil braucht nicht immer **will**. Er kann auch auffordern oder anbieten: **If you see Jack, tell him.** (Wenn du Jack siehst, sag es ihm.) **If you're tired, we can stop.** (Wenn du müde bist, können wir stehen bleiben.) **If you want to walk, you should take a map.** (Wenn du zu Fuß gehen willst, solltest du eine Karte mitnehmen.) Der Teil mit **if** bleibt im Präsens.
say.it: L'altra parte non ha sempre **will**. Può anche dire di fare o offrire: **If you see Jack, tell him.** (Se vedi Jack, diglielo.) **If you're tired, we can stop.** (Se sei stanc{m:o|f:a}, possiamo fermarci.) **If you want to walk, you should take a map.** (Se vuoi andare a piedi, dovresti prendere una cartina.) La parte con **if** resta al presente.
say.en: The other half needn't have **will**. It can tell or offer: **If you see Jack, tell him.** **If you're tired, we can stop.** **If you want to walk, you should take a map.** The **if** half stays in the present.

exercises.text: — If the weather ___ (be) good tomorrow, we'll walk to the tarn. — And if it ___ (rain)? — If it rains, we ___ (stay) at the inn. When we ___ (get) back, Mrs Birkett will make soup. — I ___ (not) come if you start at six! — If you ___ (not want) to get up early, you can come later. And if you ___ (see) Jack, tell him.

translation.sl: — Če bo jutri lepo vreme, gremo peš do jezerca. — Kaj pa, če bo deževalo? — Če bo deževalo, ostanemo v gostilni. Ko se vrnemo, bo gospa Birkett skuhala juho. — Jaz ne pridem, če začnete ob šestih! — Če nočeš zgodaj vstati, lahko prideš pozneje. In če vidiš Jacka, mu povej.
translation.de: — Wenn morgen schönes Wetter ist, gehen wir zum Bergsee. — Und wenn es regnet? — Wenn es regnet, bleiben wir im Gasthaus. Wenn wir zurückkommen, macht Mrs Birkett Suppe. — Ich komme nicht, wenn ihr um sechs losgeht! — Wenn du nicht früh aufstehen willst, kannst du später kommen. Und wenn du Jack siehst, sag es ihm.
translation.it: — Se domani è bel tempo, andiamo a piedi al laghetto. — E se piove? — Se piove, restiamo alla locanda. Quando torniamo, Mrs Birkett farà la zuppa. — Io non vengo se partite alle sei! — Se non vuoi alzarti presto, puoi venire più tardi. E se vedi Jack, diglielo.
translation.en: — If the weather is good tomorrow, we'll walk to the tarn. — And if it rains? — If it rains, we will stay at the inn. When we get back, Mrs Birkett will make soup. — I won't come if you start at six! — If you don't want to get up early, you can come later. And if you see Jack, tell him.
